title: How Much To Save Monthly To Reach $1 Million by Retirement Age
description: The definitive 'Millionaire Calculator' by starting age.
content:
One million dollars is the classic retirement benchmark. While inflation means it buys less than it used to, it remains the gold standard for financial security. The good news is that hitting $1M is a math problem, not a magic trick. The variables are: Time, Contribution, and Rate of Return. The earlier you start, the less you have to save. This guide breaks down the exact monthly dollar amount you need to invest to hit $1,000,000 by age 65.

Key Takeaways

  • Start Early: At age 20, you need less than $200/month. At age 50, you need nearly $3,000/month. The 'Cost of Waiting' is exponential.
  • The 10% Assumption: The S&P 500 averages ~10% nominal returns. Using this average, we can project growth. (Use 7% if you want to adjust for inflation/purchasing power).
  • Consistency Matters: These numbers assume you never stop contributing and never withdraw. Interrupting compounding destroys the result.
  • Tax Advantages: Using a 401(k) or Roth IRA makes this easier because you aren't losing 15-20% of your growth to taxes every year.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The contribution limit for a 401(k) ($23,500) plus an IRA ($7,000) gives you over $30,000 of annual tax-advantaged space. You have plenty of room to hit these targets.

The Monthly Targets (to hit $1M by 65)

Assuming 8% average annual return (conservative equity portfolio).

Starting in your 20s

  • Age 20: $190 / month. (Doable with a part-time job).
  • Age 25: $285 / month. (Doable with 401k match).

Starting in your 30s

  • Age 30: $435 / month.
  • Age 35: $670 / month. (Maxing a Roth IRA gets you close).

Starting in your 40s

  • Age 40: $1,050 / month.
  • Age 45: $1,700 / month. (Requires maxing 401k).

Starting Late (The Sprint)

  • Age 50: $3,000 / month.
  • Age 55: $5,500 / month. (Very hard. Need high income + Catch-Up contributions).

How to Automate It

  1. Set the Floor: Pick your number from the list above. Round it up.
  2. The 'Match' Hack: If your employer matches 4% of your $60k salary, that's $200/mo you don't have to save yourself. Subtract it from your target.
  3. Split the Difference: Don't put it all in one account. Put $583/mo in Roth IRA and the rest in 401(k).
  4. Increase Annually: Set a 1% auto-increase. If you start at $300/mo and increase by 10% a year, you will hit $2 Million, not $1 Million.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is $1M enough?

It provides $40,000/year in income (4% rule). Plus Social Security ($25k-$35k), that is a $70k/year retirement. For most, yes.

What if the market crashes?

Keep buying. The $1M goal relies on 30 years of average returns, which includes crashes. Buying during the crash accelerates your timeline.

Can I catch up?

Yes, but you trade time for money. You have to save massive amounts later to make up for small amounts earlier.
